newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia rice yields forecast at 3.4 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia rice yields forecast at 3.4 mln tonnes.

text.p: Cambodia is expected to achieve a rice surplus for the second year in a row in 1997, with yields likely to soar 35 percent higher than the average for the past five years, an independent audit has revealed.

The joint assessment by the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation and World Food Programme was released late on Wednesday. It found that despite severe flooding in much of Cambodia in late 1996, the 1996/97 rice crop will likely reach 2,733,000 tonnes of wet season paddy and 657,000 tonnes for dry season irrigated crops.

The total of 3,390,000 tonnes would represent a two percent increase over the previous year's crops and a five percent increase over the average for the past five years, said the report from the two agencies.
The rice surplus is expected to be 127,000 tonnes.
"Cambodia is definitely making structural progress in food production, although it has not fully overcome its crucial problem of food shortages," said the report.

The report, based on a survey of six provinces in January, said nearly 20 percent of communes in the 18 main rice-growing provinces needed food aid, and it urged the need for better irrigation and road systems for transporting commodities.
Despite the continuing pockets of rice shortages, the report was good news for the Cambodia, which had nearly 250,000 hectares of rice crops flooded last October.

But rice yields were less severely hurt than originally expected, leading the government earlier this week to revise 1996 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth to 6.5 percent from the initially reported six percent.
Cambodia's economy is heavily agrarian, with agriculture representing 80 percent of all jobs and 40 percent of GDP, but the sector accounts for less than one-fifth of total exports.
